name: McCart

nadir.desc: The property consists of a single-story primary residence with a dark gray roof|A side carport extends from the house with multiple vehicles parked underneath and in front|Several white-roofed structures and covered enclosures occupy the rear yard|Additional small buildings are present toward the back of the lot|Tall evergreen trees and bare trees frame the property|Open grassy areas and garden beds are visible between the structures|Wooden fencing encloses the lot.

alpha.desc: The front of the residence shows a single-story house with a dark gray roof and a side carport|Multiple vehicles are parked under and in front of the carport|Tall evergreen trees stand along one side of the property|A wooden fence are visible going down the right perimeter|Open grassy area make up the front yard.

bravo.desc: The left side of the residence shows the side of the house and carport|Multiple white-roofed structures and covered enclosures are visible in the rear yard|Bare trees and wooden fencing continue along the perimeter

charlie.desc: The rear of the residence shows the back of the house and a cluster of white-roofed structures and small buildings|Open grassy areas and garden beds fill the spaces around the structures|Tall trees frame the rear of the lot|Wooden fencing encloses the back portion of the property.

delta.desc: The right side of the residence shows the side of the house, carport, and multiple vehicles parked along the driveway|White-roofed structures continue into the rear yard|Grass area runs along the right perimeter in the backyard|Wooden fencing and a gate are visible near the front|Tall evergreen trees stand on one side of the lot|Road access leads directly into the side parking area.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided from the street into a side driveway and carport that runs along the house. Multiple vehicles occupy the carport and driveway area. A cluster of white-roofed structures and small buildings fills much of the rear yard and may limit open movement behind the house. Tall evergreen trees and bare trees frame both sides of the property. Wooden fencing and a front gate enclose the lot. The property sits on a narrow, deep urban lot with neighboring residences on both sides.
clarifications: Does the side carport and driveway continue through to the rear yard, or does it end at the house? What is the primary use of the multiple white-roofed structures and covered enclosures in the rear? Is the front gate locked or restricted during normal hours? Can emergency vehicles or personnel move around the house on the tree-lined side? Are any of the rear structures used as living space or storage only?
